A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReDi study and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally contains Appendices A–G. The supplied material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, including conditional and unconditional results, representation guidance, and dimensionality-reduction and token-fusion ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ReDi+REPA results, throughput measurements, detailed checkpoint evaluations, and qualitative generation examples.

M1.justification: v2 adds an optional ReDi+REPA variant with an alignment objective and an eighth-layer projection MLP (Section 4.2, Appendix B.3). Core joint diffusion, PCA, token fusion, and Representation Guidance remain unchanged. Appendix A documents the SiT application already used in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on ImageNet at 256×256 for conditional and unconditional image generation. Additional checkpoints, guidance examples, and class-specific image grids remain within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The modality-fusion comparison expands from merged and separate ReDi tokens alone in v1 Table 5 to include vanilla DiT-B/2 in v2 Table 6. The main generative comparison methods in Tables 1–2 remain the same.

E3.justification: Reported long-training checkpoints change from 3M to 4M iterations in Table 1 and from 600 to 800 epochs in Table 2. v2 introduces a throughput protocol using one A100, batch size 64, and 250 sampling steps. Section 4.1 also replaces '250 function evaluations' with '250 sampling steps'; this reporting revision does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted test of combining REPA alignment with ReDi, measures throughput in the retained token-fusion analysis, and adds a qualitative Representation Guidance sweep from 1.1 to 1.6 (Figure 8). Existing PCA, CFG, and conditional/unconditional guidance analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The appendix results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds ReDi+REPA checkpoint results, fuller metrics in Tables 9–10, throughput measurements, and qualitative samples. Table 1 reports standalone ReDi FID 3.3 at 4M iterations versus 3.7 at 3M in v1; Table 2 replaces the 600-epoch FID 1.64 entry with 800-epoch FID 1.61. These are different-budget results. v2 introduces inconsistencies: its prose reports FID 1.64 and hybrid FID 3.6, whereas the corresponding tables give 1.61 and 3.5.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds continuous interpolation, a probability-flow ODE, and the joint SiT velocity objective in Equations 14–18, beyond v1's DDPM formulation. No new theorem or proof appears. The new endpoint conditions in Equation 14 conflict with the default schedules alpha_t=t and sigma_t=1−t stated in Appendix A.2.

C1.justification: The principal joint-generation, Representation Guidance, and conditional/unconditional improvement claims remain. Figure 2 extends the prominently presented acceleration claim to combining ReDi with REPA, claiming approximately 11× faster convergence than REPA, beyond v1's standalone comparisons.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets alignment and joint modeling as complementary objectives. Appendix E adds discussion of unexplored multiple visual representations and alternatives to PCA compression. Existing interpretations of dimensionality, token fusion, and guidance largely remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: loss weight lambda_z=1, dropout probability 0.2, model depths/heads/widths, AdamW learning rate and betas, eight A100 40GB GPUs, throughput measurement details, and the hybrid alignment implementation. These are principally newly disclosed settings. The direct repository link is replaced by a project-page-and-code link; its external availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly credits VideoJam's guidance approach as inspiration for Representation Guidance, whereas v1 mentioned only its joint motion representation. It adds citations to Lipman et al., Nichol and Dhariwal, and Elfwing et al., removes the Futurist and EQ-VAE citations, and expands descriptions of existing baselines.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. v2 makes local wording edits, expands the ReDi acronym, moves and elaborates baseline descriptions in Appendix D, and adds organized appendices with cross-references. This extends documentation without extensively rewriting the main narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a two-panel comparison including the hybrid model. v2 adds the hybrid table, architecture and optimization tables, detailed benchmark tables, and Figures 8–16. The former Table 5 becomes Table 6 with a baseline row and throughput column, and main-table captions move above their tables. These substantially expand and revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the experiments easier to reproduce through explicit loss, dropout, optimizer, architecture, and hardware details. The combination experiment and measured throughput also strengthen evidence about compatibility and computational cost. These useful gains extend a largely retained study, but are tempered by new table/prose FID mismatches and contradictory SiT time conventions in Appendix A.
